full_judgment: 2. The plaintiff-respondent No. 1 Srimati Anarathi Mondal instituted Title Suit No. 73 of 1983 on 2-3-1983 in the Court of Munsif now Assistant Judge, Khulna against the said defendant No. 1 and others praying for a declaration that the compromise decree dated 21-6-1962 passed in the earlier Title Suit No. 182 of 1962 of the 1st Court of Munsif, Khulna filed by the said defendant No. 1 against the respondent No. 1 is forged, fraudulent, collusive and not binding upon her (respondent No. 1) stating to the effect that the suit land belonged to her father Bisturam Gain and RS and SA Khatian were correctly recorded in her father's name; that the said defendant No. 1 Kartic Chandra Sarker was a village quack and a litigant person of the locality. The plaintiffs father died leaving behind her as only daughter and 3 grandsons to inherit properties left by said Bishuram; that plaintiff possessed the suit land on payment of rent. But when the plaintiffs son Bimal went to pay rent in the year 1983 he was surprised to see the name of Kartic Chandra Sarker defendant No. 1 in the record of right in place of her father Bisturam Gain; that on an inquiry it was detected that said defendant No.1 mutated his name in Miscellaneous Case No. 22 of 1978-79 on the basis of a compromise decree dated 21-6-1962 passed in Title Suit No. 182 of 1962. Against the present respondent No. 1; that plaintiff respondent never received any summons or notice as defendant and she did not compromise the suit by putting her thumb impression in any application of compromise. The alleged compromise decree was obtained by practicing fraud. The defendant No. 1 contested the instant suit by filing written statement denying the material allegations contending, inter alia, that the suit land belonged to Bisturam Gain, father of the respondent No. 1. But said Bisturam settled the suit land orally to him (defendant No. 1) and subsequently, granted an 'Amalnama' in Jaistha 1356 BS; that Bisturam also granted him rent receipt and delivered possession of the suit land. During SA operation the name of Bisturam was wrongly recorded in the SA Khatian and the plaintiff respondent as daughter of Bisturam was claiming the suit land and, as such, the said defendant No. 1 (predecessor of leave-petitioners) had to file Title Suit No. 182 of 1962 and that suit was compromised between the respondent No. 1 and the defendant No. 1 (predecessor of the present petitioners). The compromise was genuine and defendant No. 1 has been in possession of the suit land for long over 12 years and thereby acquired a valid title in the suit land.
